CanBeGeneratedInCombat.maps_to: NOT PORTED -- the sim sets `can_be_generated_by_modifiers = False` instead (knowledge_curses.py:26)
CanBeGeneratedInCombat.issue: `public override bool CanBeGeneratedInCombat => false` (Disintegration.cs:16) has no counterpart: the sim leaves `can_be_generated_in_combat` at its True default and instead turns OFF a DIFFERENT flag, `can_be_generated_by_modifiers`, which Disintegration.cs does not override at all (C# leaves it `=> true`, CardModel.cs:648). Two mismatched flags in one card. DORMANT both ways: the in-combat generators the first flag gates (Infernal Blade, Discovery, Jack of All Trades, Distraction) all draw from `pool_card_ids()`, which is built from IRONCLAD_POOL and contains no Status cards, and the second flag gates the random-CURSE pool, which a Status of Status rarity is not in either. Live for the first flag the moment any in-combat generator is pointed at a pool that includes statuses.

ctor.issue: STATUS / STATUS / NONE map exactly, and the sim's shared `_ChoosableCurse` base carries them for all four Knowledge-Demon cards. The canonical energy cost is -1 in C# and 0 in the sim. `CardEnergyCost.GetWithModifiers` returns early on `_base < 0` (CardEnergyCost.cs:100-103), so the game's unplayable card is immune to every cost modifier and keeps reporting -1; the sim runs a base of 0 through the full modifier chain (cards/base.py:222-232). `GetAmountToSpend()` clamps to Math.Max(0, ...) on both sides, so only what is READ diverges. Same mechanism and same verdict as card/ascenders_bane's ctor entry (rule 3). DORMANT: the ported cost readers all filter `> 0` or skip `<= 1` (relics/mummified_hand.py:25, potions.py:168, cards/event_cards.py:328), and events/infested_automaton.py:35 filters pool_card_ids(), which holds no curses or statuses.

CanonicalVars.rationale: `new PowerVar<DisintegrationPower>(6m)` (Disintegration.cs:18) == `default_power_amount = 6`, copied into `self.power_amount` by `_init_vars` so it is re-seeded on downgrade. The sim's comment notes the amount scales 6/7/8 with the Curse of Knowledge counter, which is the Knowledge Demon's business, not the card's.

OnChosen.maps_to: _ChoosableCurse's power application via CombatState.select_cards (knowledge_curses.py module docstring; the applier is the Knowledge Demon monster)
OnChosen.rationale: `PowerCmd.Apply<DisintegrationPower>(new ThrowingPlayerChoiceContext(), Owner.Creature, DynamicVars["DisintegrationPower"].BaseValue, Owner.Creature, this)` (Disintegration.cs:25-28) == the sim's select-then-apply path, which reads `power_cls` and `power_amount` off the chosen card and applies it to the player. Self-target, self-applier, amount 6 on both sides. `KnowledgeDemon.IChoosable` is an interface, not a CardModel override, so the harness's `public override` scan does not enumerate it -- added by hand.

OnPlay.rationale: Disintegration.cs declares no OnPlay, so playing it would do nothing. See the guard for the playability flag.

guards.what: the sim marks the card `is_playable = False` (knowledge_curses.py:23); Disintegration.cs declares NO Unplayable keyword
guards.issue: C# gives this Status no CanonicalKeywords at all, so in the game it is a PLAYABLE no-effect Status -- the same shape as card/beckon, which the sim does model as playable. DORMANT: the four Knowledge-Demon cards are never added to a pile on either side (the sim's module docstring and C#'s OnChosen-only design agree), so nothing can ever try to play one. Live the moment any of them reaches a combat pile -- which is exactly what a ported "add a random Status to your hand" effect would do.
